quote: SNAP-ACCELERATION SMOKE TEST PROCEDURE FOR HEAVY-DUTY DIESEL POWERED VEHICLES
source_value: SAE J1667 is the heavy-duty diesel snap-acceleration smoke procedure; it states no petrol two-speed idle rpm band
note: The band itself is right: 40 CFR 85.2215 (S011) runs the high-speed mode with engine speed between 2200 and 2800 rpm. The BAR citation was not fetched. Fix: cite 40 CFR 85.2215 in place of SAE J1667.

quote: 2500 ±300 rpm, with transmission in neutral
note: Text on the S011 page, at the tail of the section before 85.2215 (a two-speed test that then reduces speed to idle); 85.2215 itself gives a 2200-2800 rpm window centred on 2500.

quote: must not exceed 3.5 % at the setting used for the type I test and must not exceed 4.5 % within the range of adjustments
source_value: Euro 1 type II test: idle CO <= 3.5 % at the type I setting; 4.5 % only as the maximum within the adjustment range
note: 4.5 % is a real 91/441/EEC value but not the as-set idle limit (3.5 %). In UK in-service testing 4.5 % is the non-cat limit for cars first used 1/8/75 to 1/8/86 (S009), not a cat-car limit.

quote: From 1/8/95 and before 31/8/2 but are not included in the Annex | 0.5% vol
source_value: 0.5 % at natural idle is the UK in-service limit for cat cars first used 1/8/95 to 31/8/2002; Euro 2 type-approval (94/12/EC) sets no idle CO limit beyond the 91/441 type II values (3.5 % / 4.5 %)
note: Value right, attribution wrong: the line labels it a type-approval limit. 94/12/EC (fetched, not cited) amends the type I g/km limits; it does not amend the type II test.

quote: From 1/8/95 and before 31/8/2 but are not included in the Annex | 0.5% vol | No requirement | No specific requirement but engine must not be clearly above its normal idling speed | 0.3% | 0.02% vol (200ppm)
source_value: HC <= 200 ppm at raised speed (2500-3000 rpm) for cat cars first used 1/8/95 to 31/8/2002
note: 1200 ppm is the non-cat natural-idle HC limit (cars first used before 1/8/92, or 1/8/92-1/8/95 not in the Annex), not a 2500 rpm limit. Euro 2 type-approval gives HC+NOx in g/km, not ppm.

quote: From 1/9/2 but are not included in the Annex | 0.3% vol
source_value: 0.3 % at natural idle applies to cars first used from 1/9/2002; Euro 3 cars first used 1/2001 to 31/8/2002 have 0.5 %
note: The UK in-service limit bands by date of first use and not by Euro class. 0.3 % holds for most Euro 3 cars but not for those first used before 1/9/2002.
200 ppm HC at raised speed holds for both UK bands that cover Euro 3 cars (1/8/95-31/8/2 and from 1/9/2).

quote: From 1/9/2 but are not included in the Annex | 0.3% vol
source_value: 0.3 % CO at natural idle for cars first used from 1/9/2002; 0.2 % is the raised-speed (2500-3000 rpm) limit
note: The line puts the fast-idle value in the idle column. S001 gives the same pair: CO up to 0.3% at idle, 0.2% at fast idle.
Row for cars first used from 1/9/2002: HC 200 ppm at raised speed.

quote: at engine idle: 0,3 % (7)
source_value: Idle CO 0.3 % and high idle CO 0.2 % for vehicles under footnote (7) which names Regulation (EC) No 715/2007 Annex I Table 1 (Euro 5)
note: Euro 5 type-approval sets no idle CO limit: Regulation 692/2008 Annex IV (S008) only records the type 2 idle values. The line labels 0.2 % a type-approval idle ceiling; 0.2 % is the high-idle roadworthiness value.

quote: measuring carbon monoxide emissions at idling speeds (normal and high)
source_value: Euro 5 type 2 test covers CO only and sets no idle HC limit; 200 ppm HC is the UK in-service raised-speed limit (S009)
note: Value right as an in-service (MOT) limit, attribution to type-approval wrong.

quote: With effect from 1 January 2011
source_value: Euro 5: new types from 1 September 2009; all new vehicles (registration, sale) from 1 January 2011
note: Start year right, end year wrong: Euro 5 applies to all new M1 cars from 2011, not 2010. S007 is the legislation.gov.uk text with GB wording substituted; the dates are the EU originals.

quote: CO up to 0.3% at idle (450rpm to 1,500rpm)
source_value: Legal idle CO limit 0.3 % for the wiki's Euro 4 baseline; the normal-range upper edge 0.45 % exceeds it
note: README rule: a normal range above a legal limit is CONTRADICTED. For cat cars first used 1/8/95-31/8/2002 the UK idle limit is 0.5 % (S009), so 0.45 % is legal for those; see Disputes.

quote: From 1/8/86 and before 1/8/92 | 3.5% vol
source_value: For 1990-1998 cars: non-cat 3.5 % (first used from 1/8/86), early cat 0.5 % (1/8/95 to 31/8/2002); 4.5 % applies only to cars first used before 1/8/86
note: The 0.5 % end holds; the 4.5 % end is the pre-1986 non-cat value, outside the stated 1990-1998 era. Euro 1 type-approval uses 3.5 % at the set point (S005).

quote: CO up to 0.3% at idle (450rpm to 1,500rpm)
source_value: Legal idle CO limit 0.3 %; the marginal band starts at 0.45 %, so 0.30-0.45 % (an MOT fail) sits in Ideal
note: Lower edge contradicted by the legal limit; the 1.0 % upper edge is a GASLab design value with no outside source.

note: UK basic emissions test; the same 0.3 % is the default for cars first used from 1/9/2002 (S009).
